screenings.title: White Nights
screenings.description: Italy, 1957 Directed by Luchino Visconti Based on the short story by Fyodor Dostoevsky Starring Marcello Mastroianni, Maria Schell, Jean Marais Music by Nino Rota In Italian with English subtitles Approx 103 min. “Visconti’s version of the Dostoevsky story—about the chance encounter of a couple as she is waiting in vain for her lover, and the obsessive, panic-stricken relationship which then develops between them—later filmed by Bresson as FOUR NIGHTS OF A DREAMER. screenings.title: Sheep in the Box
screenings.description: Two years after losing their son Kakeru, Otone and her husband Kensuke take into their lives a humanoid from a company that rents humanoids to bereaved families as replacements for lost loved ones. The robot looks and behaves exactly like Kakeru, with Otone embracing its arrival as Kensuke struggles to accept it. Living with “him” seems to restore the flow of time within the family, yet gradually exposes the unspoken wounds and lingering regrets each parent carries after the loss. All the while, he begins to slip away to meet other humanoid children, unnoticed by the parents.

screenings.title: Center Stage
screenings.description: Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Stanley Kwan Starring Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English Approx. 155 min. International superstar Maggie Cheung (IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu, known as the “Greta Garbo of China,” in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan (ROUGE). Praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence, Ruan’s private life, which was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids, began to mirror the melodramas which brought her fame, culminating in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid, and almost overwhelmingly moving” (Time Out). Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy by L'Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Sherman's March
screenings.description: U.S., 1986 Written and directed by Ross McElwee Approx. 158 min. Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South. A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, Sherman’s March sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross’s deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross’s mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel. A landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV. A Little Field Films Restoration with support from Cinema Conservancy, Harvard Film Archive, and The Library of Congress. Restoration Produced by Mark Meatto. Restoration Supervised by Ross McElwee. screenings.title: Happy Together
screenings.description: Hong Kong cinema superstars Tony Leung and Leslie Cheung play a pair of lovers living out the waning days of their relationship as expatriates in Buenos Aires. Lusty tango bars, the salsa music of the La Boca sidewalks, and a hypnotic visit to the nearby Iguazu Falls give further dimension to the tensions growing between the two. Winner of the Best Director prize at the 1997 Cannes Film Festival, Wong’s Happy Together is a stunning display of filmmaking style and a touching story of love on the brink of dissolution.

screenings.title: The Bakery Girl of Monceau + Suzanne's Career
screenings.description: Though rightfully an international arthouse phenomenon, Rohmer’s Moral Tales are remarkable in just how little they scream for attention, notable for their modesty of scale and their dedication to delicate observation rather than anything resembling firebrand provocation. The first two entries in the series are perfect instances of this: in The Bakery Girl of Monceau, a law student (a young Barbet Schroeder) flirts brazenly with the title character while brooding over his romantic failure with another girl; in Suzanne’s Career, in which two young men, a woman-shy introvert and a self-styled Don Juan, get mixed up with—and, in their individual ways, misuse—independent minded Catherine Sée, only to find their egos far more fragile than hers. Not exactly “high concept” stuff on the page, but on the screen… an abundance.

screenings.title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
screenings.description: If poetry had a pop icon, Mary Oliver would be it. Celebrated bestseller, Pulitzer Prize winner, lover of dogs and long walks in the woods, openly queer but intensely private, Oliver was America’s unlikely contemporary mystic, stalking the ponds and forests of Cape Cod for nearly 50 years in order to open herself – and her readers – to the known and unknowable world. From a lonely childhood to literary fame, Oliver’s life was shaped by devotion to nature, paying attention, and the long journey toward learning to love and to be loved. Her poems inspire liberals and conservatives, atheists and believers, naturalists and urbanites, speaking directly to contemporary anxieties about attention, presence, and the human relationship with the natural world – issues that feel especially pressing in an era of climate crisis, digital distraction, and social fragmentation.

screenings.title: The Invite
screenings.description: Joe (Seth Rogen) and Angela’s (Olivia Wilde) marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors (Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton) for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places. Have they reignited the spark or lit the match that burns it all down? A remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs, Olivia Wilde’s star-studded take on a dinner party dramedy (written by Will McCormack and Rashida Jones) is a timely portrait of a modern marriage, teeming with wit, belly laughs, and a surprising poignancy.

screenings.title: My Night at Maud's
screenings.description: Rohmer’s first feature-length entry in his “Six Moral Tales” series (following The Bakery Girl of Monceau and Suzanne’s Career) stars Jean-Louis Trintignant as a conscientious Catholic bachelor who is sorely tempted when he meets charming divorcée Françoise Fabian. Néstor Almendros’s black-and-white photography crystallizes the atmosphere of a damp Christmastime in mid-1960s central France while Rohmer exactingly depicts middle-class morals buckling under pressure as the sexual revolution arrives in the provinces.

screenings.title: Aferim!
screenings.description: Jude won Best Director from a Berlin jury for this, his third feature, a meticulously detailed, ribald evocation of 19th-century Romania evoking Cervantes and Rabelais as well as the American horse opera, and shot in tactilely textured black and white, following a blundering constable (Teodor Corban) and his weedy son as they trail a fugitive—a runaway Roma slave accused of rape by a grandee living in the cop’s jurisdiction—across the countryside of Wallachia. “Combine[s] the best pleasures of historical romp, road movie, and Western… A rich plundering of the language and prejudices of its time that makes you gasp and laugh despite yourself.” —Sight & Sound

Visconti traps his characters (three excellent performances) within a claustrophobic canal-side set, and the film is a series of brief walks, chases, attempted escapes, always frustrated. Shot as neo-realist high tragedy, the film offers its characters only one strange moment of escape from their night-time obsessions—a raucous, sexual, subversive scene in a dance-hall. Then the snow comes down, and with it a chilly desperation about the extent of human self-delusion.” – Time Out Restored by Luce Cinecittà, from the original 35mm negative Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: A Sad and Beautiful World
screenings.description: In this sweeping love story that spans three decades of passion, heartbreak and hope, Nino and Yasmina find themselves drawn together by a magnetic relationship. As they face an impossible choice between love and survival, they must decide if they want to build a family and chart a path to happiness in Lebanon, despite the tragedies ravaging the country. In Arabic with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Center Stage
screenings.description: Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Stanley Kwan Starring Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English Approx. 155 min. International superstar Maggie Cheung (IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu, known as the “Greta Garbo of China,” in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan (ROUGE). Praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence, Ruan’s private life, which was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids, began to mirror the melodramas which brought her fame, culminating in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid, and almost overwhelmingly moving” (Time Out). Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy by L'Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Highway Hypnosis
screenings.description: Between the years of 1974 to 1979, not long after Manson Family trials had concluded, enigmatic artist and connoisseur of fringe culture, John Aes-Nihil, embarked on a project to “re-stage” the events leading up to the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders as a series of faux home movies, based on the legend that the Family had at one point stolen camera equipment to document their actions. The resulting feature— which, coincidentally, premiered in 1984 at EZTV alongside HIGHWAY HYPNOSIS— truly lives up to its filmmaker’s namesake Aesthetic Nihilism: Shot entirely on Super8mm and completely silent save for an accompanying soundtrack mostly comprised of music made by the Family itself (plus a little Patty Duke for good measure). The film re-frames the Manson Family story as a first-person travelogue across Southern California, imbued with chillingly realistic detail as we bear (false) witness to one of the most notorious events of the American century.

screenings.title: Bouchra
screenings.description: Multihyphenate artists Barki and Bennani’s playful animation/live-action hybrid film à clef offers up a delightfully idiosyncratic look at the travails of the queer expat artist. The title character here is imagined as an anthropomorphic jackal inhabiting a New York City filled with other like critters, a young filmmaker simultaneously dealing with creative crises, her rocky relationship with her mother back in Casablanca, and the pleasures and perils of sex in the city. Drawing on real phone calls and myriad other correspondences, with voice talent courtesy of the directing duo’s friends and family members, this lay-it-on-the-line autofiction is at once startlingly light on its feet and densely layered with insight, not least into the feelings that come of shakily straddling two cultures while belonging fully to neither.

screenings.title: The Asphalt Jungle
screenings.description: Possibly the best crime drama ever filmed, this taut, gritty caper begins with a meticulously planned robbery executed with clockwork precision. But bit by bit, unanticipated events and the criminal’s character flaws begin to unravel a seemingly perfect heist. A young Marilyn Monroe is featured in a small, but star-making performance. Nominated for four Academy Awards including Huston’s second for Best Director, The Asphalt Jungle would go on to influence countless crime pictures, including those of French director Jean-Pierre Melville, who declared it a masterpiece.

screenings.title: Sheep in the Box
screenings.description: Two years after losing their son Kakeru, Otone and her husband Kensuke take into their lives a humanoid from a company that rents humanoids to bereaved families as replacements for lost loved ones. The robot looks and behaves exactly like Kakeru, with Otone embracing its arrival as Kensuke struggles to accept it. Living with “him” seems to restore the flow of time within the family, yet gradually exposes the unspoken wounds and lingering regrets each parent carries after the loss. All the while, he begins to slip away to meet other humanoid children, unnoticed by the parents.

screenings.title: Wild Inside
screenings.description: Also playing: the 14-minute documentary short DREAM OF BIRDS screens with the 11:00am shows of WILD INSIDE Friday, July 31-Thursday August 6 only. Following a unique study led by Argentine physicist Gabriel Mindlin, DREAM OF BIRDS playfully explores the mystery of music through the mathematical patterns behind birdsong, and how our lives and relationships are rhythmically organized.

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: Willem Dafoe is Ed Saxberger, a postal worker whose former life as a downtown poet in late-70s New York is rediscovered by a young admirer (Donovan) and his “Enthusiasm Society,” a group of 20-somethings with a comically romanticized sense of the past. In the company of his new friends, including the mysterious and mercurial Gloria (Lee of PAST LIVES), Ed has the uncanny feeling of merging with his younger self. Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY DECEMBER), LATE FAME is a funny, lively, poignant, and occasionally haunting New York story. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film 2025 96 MIN. USA MAGNOLIA PICTURES

screenings.title: Dread Beat an Blood
screenings.description: About DREAD BEAT AN BLOOD: “[A] gem... a portrait of the artist as principled activist.” – Sasha Frere-Jones, 4Columns “Fantastic... An amazing snapshot of the time of the pre-Brixton riots... This is so relevant a movie. That’s what makes it so good.” – Gilles Peterson, BBC “A fascinating document of LKJ in his time and place, touring with the sound systems, strolling through the market and visiting Tulse Hill schools, vividly capturing black British culture in a country on the cusp of Thatcherism, just a few months before the Brixton uprising.” – Stephen Troussé, Uncut “An invaluable document of Brixton, an area that was already at the front lines of the anti-racist struggle, the streets in which people would soon rise up in rebellion. That sense of latent frustration simmers in every frame. It is Johnson himself who articulates that frustration, honing that anger into art via his poetry.” – Kevin Mccaighy, The Quietus About Linton Kwesi Johnson: “If any young artists need to know about longevity and integrity, Linton Kwesi Johnson is the one to look to... He knew his path and he walked it. His words are still relevant and that reggae bass is still vibrating.” – Steve McQueen “Linton Kwesi Johnson’s impact on the cultural landscape over the last half-century has been colossal and multi-generational.” – The Guardian “He’s written the anthems for a generation who felt oppressed and victimized... He’s now celebrated as one of this country’s most influential cultural commentators.” – BBC “A revolutionary poet for our times.” – Jacobin “The Poet Laureate of Black Britain.” – Paul Gilroy “The roots of hip-hop run deep, and among the deepest branches remains Linton Kwesi Johnson, the Jamaican-born, British-raised poet, writer, and performer often hailed as the father of dub poetry.” – David Browne, Rolling Stone

screenings.title: The Odyssey (DCP)
screenings.description: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War.

screenings.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
screenings.description: Mann’s genre-defining serial-killer thriller returns in a stunning new restoration overseen by the filmmaker himself. A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a murderer and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). Adapted from the first of Thomas Harris’s Lecktor novels, MANHUNTER’s supporting cast includes Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen.

screenings.title: Basic Instinct
screenings.description: The film that made a star of Sharon Stone, seen to good effect in Verhoeven’s previous Carolco production, Total Recall, and that also provided the studio a succès de scandale windfall. Perfectly poised as she negotiates her way through the most infamous police station interrogation scene in cinema, Stone’s pulp novelist-and-suspected ice pick murderess Catherine Trammell is a blonde ice queen à la Hitchcock who begins to melt in the arms of besotted SFPD Detective Nick Curran (Michael Douglas)—or does she only appear to? A work of carnivorous carnality that moves with prowling panther sleekness, its career-best Jerry Goldsmith score adding immeasurably to the undercurrent of imminent danger.

screenings.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
screenings.description: Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he’s devoted himself entirely to protecting his city — a full-time Spider-Man — but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

screenings.title: Barrio Triste
screenings.description: Medellin, 1987. A group of teen outcasts steals a news camera to document every detail of their dangerous lives. The first feature from acclaimed photographer and Bad Bunny music video director Stillz redefines the found footage genre as a haunting, poignant coming-of-age story with a disturbing twist. Set to an awe-inspiring score by Arca and produced by Harmony Korine’s collective EDGLRD, the film taps into the anxieties of a youth culture from the margins of history yearning to be understood.
screenings.country: Barrio Triste Crime, Drama, Fantasy, Horror

screenings.title: Stalking Chernobyl
screenings.description: After showcasing two of her documentaries last year, Spectacle is proud to host the New York City premiere of iara lee’s latest feature, THE SAMI SONG OF SURVIVAL. Throughout her prolific career as a cultural film essayist, iara lee intentionally sought out Indigenous voices in political peril. Inspired by her 2010 documentary and participation in the Gaza Freedom Flotilla, iara lee established the Cultures of Resistance Network to raise awareness of folks on the margins and the art they create. With lee’s latest, THE SAMI SONG OF SURVIVAL, we’re witnesses to the Sami people, an Indigenous group based in Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Russia. Undergoing constant oppression against imperial forces and racist colonialism, with one Sami man in particular hypothesizing, “Art could be a weapon”. A motivating mantra that sums up the essence of iara lee’s filmmaking ethos, Spectacle Theater will be screening this alongside two power-defying docs: K2 & THE INVISIBLE FOOTMEN and STALKING CHERNOBYL.

screenings.title: Jimmy
screenings.description: Shot in dreamy 16mm black and white, Yasshadai Owens’ debut feature Jimmy offers an intimate, speculative portrait of what a young James Baldwin may have experienced during his first trip to Paris in 1948. (credit: Toronto International Film Festival)

screenings.title: The Big Cheese
screenings.description: A scrappy team of eccentric American cheesemongers defies tradition to take on the world’s top cheese masters at the Mondial du Fromage, battling cultural clashes, personal struggles, and melting cheese in pursuit of respect, redemption, and a historic victory.

screenings.title: A Child of My Own
screenings.description: This new hybrid documentary from the Oscar-nominated director of The Mole Agent and The Eternal Memory follows the shocking tale of a woman desperate for a baby. Burdened by family and societal expectations, she fakes a pregnancy and gets tangled up in a crime.

screenings.title: The Fence
screenings.description: A vast public works project in West Africa. Horn (Matt Dillon), the construction site manager, and Cal (Tom Blyth), a young engineer, share lodging behind the double gates of their compound. Leone (Mia McKenna-Bruce), Horn’s recent bride, comes to join them the same night that a man (Isaach De Bankole) appears at the fence. His name is Alboury. Like a specter in the darkness, he demands the body of his brother who died earlier that day on the site. He will hound the two men all night long until they return it, as Leone watches the disaster play out before her.

screenings.title: Remake
screenings.description: “McElwee is a practitioner of cinema at its most elemental. He’s a man with a movie camera, pointing it at whatever or whoever is around him—which for many years included Adrian—and finding wellsprings of humor, truth, surprise... REMAKE shows him still to be a formidable artist in the face of tragedy, and one whose comically askew sensibility remains intact.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Extraordinarily clear-eyed for a work so broken-hearted: at once a home movie, an intimate diary, and an expansive study of the filmmaker’s purpose, constantly disrupting its own conclusions with expressions of anger, amusement, and still-unresolved confusion.” – Guy Lodge, Variety “Incorporation of his late son’s own footage elevates this beautiful, tragic movie from powerful to profound... Each of Ross McElwee’s deeply personal documentaries is built directly atop a fault line that separates—or connects—the microcosmic and the universal. But few films could be more unsparingly intimate than REMAKE.” – Elizabeth Weitzman, The Wrap “Emotionally piercing... meaningful and poignant.” –Warren Cantrell, The Playlist “A complex, layered contemplation of grief, memory, family ties and the meaning of filmmaking as a profoundly personal activity, REMAKE is a richly rewarding experience—emotionally, narratively and philosophically.” – Jonathan Romney, Screen International

screenings.title: Olmo
screenings.description: Olmo just wants to be a normal teenager and hang out with his best friend, but he must help care for his bedridden father. When Olmo gets invited to a party by his beautiful neighbor, he will do whatever he can to meet up with her while embarking on an adventure of mischief, laughs, and chaos. As the night unfolds, he may come to love the very place he’s spent so long trying to escape: his home. In English and Spanish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Julian
screenings.description: Fleur and Julian fall madly in love and decide to get married in all countries where they, as two women, are allowed to do so. But after only four marriages, their journey comes to a painful and unexpected halt.

screenings.title: Vertigo
screenings.description: Dress up becomes a matter of fevered fixation in Hitchcock’s utterly intoxicating thriller, in which ex-cop-cum-snoop-for-hire Scottie Ferguson (Jimmy Stewart) sets out on a routine job tailing the mysterious Madeline (Kim Novak), an old pal’s wife—and soon finds himself in the center of a whirlpool of romantic obsession and supernatural quandaries, speeding towards a tragic denouement. Perennially on the short list of the greatest films of all time, Hitchcock’s film of death, desire, and doppelgangers—a key inspiration haunting every frame of Chantal Akerman's La Captive—has lost none of its ability to simultaneously seduce and repel. “One of the landmarks—not merely of the movies, but of 20th-century art.”—Dave Kehr, Chicago Reader

screenings.title: Wake in Fright
screenings.description: It’s the eve of the Christmas holiday, and polite, young middle-class schoolteacher John Grant (Gary Bond), tied to a position at a tiny township in the outback, is on his way to Sydney to see his girlfriend by way of a stopoff in the grubby mining burg Bundanyabba (“The Yabba” to locals) when he pops into the pub for a drink… Five days of debauchery with local degenerates Donald Pleasence and Chips Rafferty later, the fresh-faced Grant has been replaced by a desperate, unshaven, beer-and-booze-pickled maniac, acquainted with species of depravity he could scarcely have imagined a week ago, and with the barbaric rites of the bush. A furious fever dream from Canuck director Kotcheff, who knew a thing or two about chronic self-degradation as practiced in far-flung outposts of the British Commonwealth, and one of the greatest of Australian films.

screenings.title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
screenings.description: If poetry had a pop icon, Mary Oliver would be it. Celebrated bestseller, Pulitzer Prize winner, lover of dogs and long walks in the woods, openly queer but intensely private, Oliver was America’s unlikely contemporary mystic, stalking the ponds and forests of Cape Cod for nearly 50 years in order to open herself – and her readers – to the known and unknowable world. From a lonely childhood to literary fame, Oliver’s life was shaped by devotion to nature, paying attention, and the long journey toward learning to love and to be loved. Her poems inspire liberals and conservatives, atheists and believers, naturalists and urbanites, speaking directly to contemporary anxieties about attention, presence, and the human relationship with the natural world – issues that feel especially pressing in an era of climate crisis, digital distraction, and social fragmentation.

As the night unfolds, he may come to love the very place he’s spent so long trying to escape: his home. In English and Spanish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Sherman's March
screenings.description: U.S., 1986 Written and directed by Ross McElwee Approx. 158 min. Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South. A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, Sherman’s March sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross’s deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross’s mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel. A landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV. A Little Field Films Restoration with support from Cinema Conservancy, Harvard Film Archive, and The Library of Congress. Restoration Produced by Mark Meatto. Restoration Supervised by Ross McElwee. screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. screenings.title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
screenings.description: Mann’s genre-defining serial-killer thriller returns in a stunning new restoration overseen by the filmmaker himself. A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a murderer and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). Adapted from the first of Thomas Harris’s Lecktor novels, MANHUNTER’s supporting cast includes Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen.

screenings.title: Center Stage
screenings.description: Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Stanley Kwan Starring Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English Approx. 155 min. International superstar Maggie Cheung (IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu, known as the “Greta Garbo of China,” in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan (ROUGE). Praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence, Ruan’s private life, which was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids, began to mirror the melodramas which brought her fame, culminating in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid, and almost overwhelmingly moving” (Time Out). Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy by L'Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Chocolat
screenings.description: After years of honing her craft as assistant director for the likes of Jim Jarmusch and Wim Wenders, Denis emerged as a filmmaker with a distinct and fully-formed sense of her art in this, her sensual and infinitely sensitive semi-autobiographical feature debut, drawing on memories of a childhood spent in French-occupied Africa. In Cameroon, civil servant François Cluzet comes and goes on his appointed rounds, while his young daughter and neglected wife (Giulia Boschi) gravitate ever closer to their house servant, Protée (Isaach de Bankolé) in his absence, and the murmurs of anti-colonial resistance increase in vehemence away from eavesdropping whites. “Some kind of miniature classic.”—Vincent Canby, The New York Times

screenings.title: Conversation Piece
screenings.description: Burt Lancaster reunited with his The Leopard director for Visconti’s penultimate film, an elegant odd-couple chamber drama in which the leonine “Boit” plays a graying American intellectual immured from the modern world in his Roman palazzo—until, that is, his fortress of solitude is invaded by a pushy Marquise (Silvana Mangano) who browbears him into renting her his unused top floor to be used as a gilded cage for her boytoy, Konrad (Helmut Berger), a ’68 activist turned gigolo to the gentry, who interrupts the old man’s bedtime Mozart with Italopop and nude pot parties. Best known for his work in the epic vein, Visconti here renders verbal close-combat every bit as thrilling as any dispatch from the battlefields of Europe.

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: Willem Dafoe is Ed Saxberger, a postal worker whose former life as a downtown poet in late-70s New York is rediscovered by a young admirer (Donovan) and his “Enthusiasm Society,” a group of 20-somethings with a comically romanticized sense of the past. In the company of his new friends, including the mysterious and mercurial Gloria (Lee of PAST LIVES), Ed has the uncanny feeling of merging with his younger self. Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY DECEMBER), LATE FAME is a funny, lively, poignant, and occasionally haunting New York story. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film 2025 96 MIN. USA MAGNOLIA PICTURES

screenings.title: Wild Inside
screenings.description: Also playing: the 14-minute documentary short DREAM OF BIRDS screens with the 11:00am shows of WILD INSIDE Friday, July 31-Thursday August 6 only. Following a unique study led by Argentine physicist Gabriel Mindlin, DREAM OF BIRDS playfully explores the mystery of music through the mathematical patterns behind birdsong, and how our lives and relationships are rhythmically organized.

screenings.title: White Nights
screenings.description: Italy, 1957 Directed by Luchino Visconti Based on the short story by Fyodor Dostoevsky Starring Marcello Mastroianni, Maria Schell, Jean Marais Music by Nino Rota In Italian with English subtitles Approx 103 min. “Visconti’s version of the Dostoevsky story—about the chance encounter of a couple as she is waiting in vain for her lover, and the obsessive, panic-stricken relationship which then develops between them—later filmed by Bresson as FOUR NIGHTS OF A DREAMER. Visconti traps his characters (three excellent performances) within a claustrophobic canal-side set, and the film is a series of brief walks, chases, attempted escapes, always frustrated. Shot as neo-realist high tragedy, the film offers its characters only one strange moment of escape from their night-time obsessions—a raucous, sexual, subversive scene in a dance-hall. Then the snow comes down, and with it a chilly desperation about the extent of human self-delusion.” – Time Out Restored by Luce Cinecittà, from the original 35mm negative Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: American Movie
screenings.description: The hit of the 1999 Sundance Film Festival, American Movie is the hilarious and intense story of one man’s obsession to make movies. Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, is a long way from Hollywood, but Mark Borchardt has a dream. Armed with a driving ambition and nothing to lose, the fast-talking Borchardt enlists friends, local thespians and unwilling family members to help him finish his no-budget horror film, Coven. The camera doesn’t flinch as it captures every emotional crisis and financial pitfall in his two-year odyssey. What emerges is a bizarre, yet surprisingly heartfelt, documentary portrait of a true American character.

screenings.title: A Sad and Beautiful World
screenings.description: In this sweeping love story that spans three decades of passion, heartbreak and hope, Nino and Yasmina find themselves drawn together by a magnetic relationship. As they face an impossible choice between love and survival, they must decide if they want to build a family and chart a path to happiness in Lebanon, despite the tragedies ravaging the country. In Arabic with English subtitles.

screenings.title: The Sami Song of Survival
screenings.description: After showcasing two of her documentaries last year, Spectacle is proud to host the New York City premiere of iara lee’s latest feature, THE SAMI SONG OF SURVIVAL. Throughout her prolific career as a cultural film essayist, iara lee intentionally sought out Indigenous voices in political peril. Inspired by her 2010 documentary and participation in the Gaza Freedom Flotilla, iara lee established the Cultures of Resistance Network to raise awareness of folks on the margins and the art they create. With lee’s latest, THE SAMI SONG OF SURVIVAL, we’re witnesses to the Sami people, an Indigenous group based in Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Russia. Undergoing constant oppression against imperial forces and racist colonialism, with one Sami man in particular hypothesizing, “Art could be a weapon”. A motivating mantra that sums up the essence of iara lee’s filmmaking ethos, Spectacle Theater will be screening this alongside two power-defying docs: K2 & THE INVISIBLE FOOTMEN and STALKING CHERNOBYL.

screenings.description: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War.

screenings.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
screenings.description: Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he’s devoted himself entirely to protecting his city — a full-time Spider-Man — but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

screenings.title: Amadeus (70mm)
screenings.description: Producer Paul Zaentz in person on August 9 Dir. Milos Forman. 1984, 160 mins. U.S./France. 70mm. With F. Murray Abraham, Tom Hulce, Elizabeth Berridge, Jeffrey Jones, Christine Ebersole, Simon Callow, Cynthia Nixon. Milos Forman’s thrilling, Best Picture–winning adaptation of Peter Shaffer’s play may be, without parallel, the greatest cinematic evocation of artistic jealousy, centering on the mythic rivalry between Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and Antonio Salieri in 18th-century Vienna. Court composer for Emperor Joseph II, Salieri grows increasingly resentful of the ease with which the crass, childlike musician writes his works of astonishing beauty, leading to tragedy. Personifying the timeless, fruitless struggle between genius and mediocrity, Amadeus is a film of operatic force and keen wit, featuring brilliant performances by both Tom Hulce as Mozart and especially an Oscar-winning F. Murray Abraham as his envious competitor. Buy tickets for August 7 Buy tickets for August 9 Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership.

screenings.title: Julian
screenings.description: Fleur and Julian fall madly in love and decide to get married in all countries where they, as two women, are allowed to do so. But after only four marriages, their journey comes to a painful and unexpected halt.

screenings.title: Paranoid Park
screenings.description: Adapting Blake Nelson’s Y.A. novel of the same name, Van Sant renders the youth gathering place of the skate park a voluptuous dreamscape with the help of cinematographers Chris Doyle and Rain Kathy Li. Teenaged skate rat Alex—Gabe Nevins, leading a largely amateur cast recruited via MySpace—finds himself a prime suspect in the death of a security guard, silently carrying a crushing burden of knowledge through his daily rounds, a contrast to the gravity-defying liberation he finds carving it up at “Paranoid Park.”

screenings.description: Dir. Fred Dekker. 1986, 88 mins. DCP. Tom Atkins, Jason Lively, Jill Whitlow, Allan Kayser. College becomes the stuff of nightmares when slug-like alien creatures transform an entire campus of coeds into zombies in this campy chiller written and directed by 1980s horror staple Fred Dekker (The Monster Squad). Though not as well known as other zombie films of the decade, Night of the Creeps merits revisiting thanks to its ecstatic, genre-bending celebration of B-horror films of the 1950s spiced with signature ’80s gore. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / free for MoMI members at the Senior/Student level and above. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. screenings.title: Collateral
screenings.description: Los Angeles cabbie Max Durocher (Jamie Foxx) is in for the toughest fare of his working life when he picks up one Vincent (Tom Cruise, natty in charcoal gray sharkskin suit), a jazz enthusiast and professional hitman who quite firmly insists that his driver accompany him on his evening’s rounds, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. Shooting LA exteriors after dark with a then-state-of-the-art Sony F-900 digital camera, Mann gave his film a wholly distinctive texture—combining expressionistic smear with a new ability to pick up detail that would be lost on celluloid—and initiated a quiet revolution in low-light cinematography. A drum-tight character-based thriller, and the only film in which you can see Tom Cruise saying: “Yo, homie… Is that my briefcase?”

screenings.description: This new hybrid documentary from the Oscar-nominated director of The Mole Agent and The Eternal Memory follows the shocking tale of a woman desperate for a baby. Burdened by family and societal expectations, she fakes a pregnancy and gets tangled up in a crime.

screenings.title: The French Connection
screenings.description: “1971 was a hell of a year for gritty Big Apple movies... One of the best all-around tours of New York in [the 70s].” – Jason Bailey, Flavorwire “Hard-nosed, pork-pie-hatted, vulgar, a tough cop in the latest measure of a fine tradition, [Hackman] exists neither to rise nor to fall, to excite neither pity nor terror—but to function. To function in New York City is its own heroism, and the film recognizes that.” – The New York Times “A knockout police thriller with so much jarring excitement that it almost calls for comic-book expletives. POW! ZOWIE!” – Jay Cocks “Solid, slick filmmaking, full of dirty cops, shrewd operators, and slam-bang action.” – Dave Kehr “Like an aggravated case of New York.” – Pauline Kael “Friedkin’s symphony of long, sharp shocks is memorable for any number of sequences: the cat-and-mouse subway game, the ballbusting bar shakedown, a breakneck chase scene that still seems leagues ahead of greatest-ever competitors.” – David Fear, Time Out (New York) “Fraught with urban decay and racial tension, Friedkin’s bang-bang procedural created a paradigm for the tell-it-like-it-is cop drama... While Dirty Harry provided audiences an anti-establishment legal vigilante, THE FRENCH CONNECTION introduced the notion of the heroic working-class narc. Blue-collar to the bone, Popeye lives in public housing and feeds his face with a rancid-looking slice in the course of a freezing afternoon spent staking out on the Upper East Side boîte where the French smuggler who is about to unload 100 pounds of uncut heroin leisurely consumes a multi-course feast.” – J. Hoberman, The Village Voice “In a sense, the whole movie is a chase... the smugglers and the law officers are endlessly circling and sniffing each other… Doyle himself is a bad cop, by ordinary standards; he harasses and brutalizes people, he is a racist, he endangers innocent people during the chase scene (which is a high-speed ego trip)… THE FRENCH CONNECTION is as amoral as its hero, as violent, as obsessed and as frightening.” – Roger Ebert

screenings.description: Hollywood-sleaze auteur Jared Masters is an LA based, low budget filmmaker, creating an array of women-centric features inspired by VHS slashers and 60’s B-movies. His films represent a modern take on genre films, and have John Waters/Kuchar Brothers humor to them. Jared refers to himself as a modern cult filmmaker, occasionally starring in the films he makes. The three films selected are an introduction to his filmography, highlighting his taste for camp and self-aware humor, backed by a clear love for cinema. Masters works align with the Spectacle vision to highlight underrated, seldom-viewed filmmakers and late-night summer indies.

screenings.title: The Milk of Sorrow
screenings.description: Winner of the Golden Bear at the 59th Berlin International Film Festival, Llosa’s formidable sophomore feature focuses on Fausta (Magaly Solier, in a performance nearly free of dialogue), the only daughter of an aged Indigenous Peruvian woman who, following her mother’s death, must negotiate arrangements for her burial as well as negotiate the smothering legacy of trauma that her parent, horribly misused during the Shining Path terrorist insurgencies of the 1980s and ’90s, has left behind with her child even after herself departing this mortal coil. “Littered with unforgettable images of incongruity, destruction, and, finally, healing” [The Village Voice], The Milk of Sorrow is an exquisitely shot study in inherited injury guarded like a precious heirloom, a work of tragic magic realism.

screenings.description: About DREAD BEAT AN BLOOD: “[A] gem... a portrait of the artist as principled activist.” – Sasha Frere-Jones, 4Columns “Fantastic... An amazing snapshot of the time of the pre-Brixton riots... This is so relevant a movie. That’s what makes it so good.” – Gilles Peterson, BBC “A fascinating document of LKJ in his time and place, touring with the sound systems, strolling through the market and visiting Tulse Hill schools, vividly capturing black British culture in a country on the cusp of Thatcherism, just a few months before the Brixton uprising.” – Stephen Troussé, Uncut “An invaluable document of Brixton, an area that was already at the front lines of the anti-racist struggle, the streets in which people would soon rise up in rebellion. That sense of latent frustration simmers in every frame. It is Johnson himself who articulates that frustration, honing that anger into art via his poetry.” – Kevin Mccaighy, The Quietus About Linton Kwesi Johnson: “If any young artists need to know about longevity and integrity, Linton Kwesi Johnson is the one to look to... He knew his path and he walked it. His words are still relevant and that reggae bass is still vibrating.” – Steve McQueen “Linton Kwesi Johnson’s impact on the cultural landscape over the last half-century has been colossal and multi-generational.” – The Guardian “He’s written the anthems for a generation who felt oppressed and victimized... He’s now celebrated as one of this country’s most influential cultural commentators.” – BBC “A revolutionary poet for our times.” – Jacobin “The Poet Laureate of Black Britain.” – Paul Gilroy “The roots of hip-hop run deep, and among the deepest branches remains Linton Kwesi Johnson, the Jamaican-born, British-raised poet, writer, and performer often hailed as the father of dub poetry.” – David Browne, Rolling Stone

screenings.title: The Fence
screenings.description: A vast public works project in West Africa. Horn (Matt Dillon), the construction site manager, and Cal (Tom Blyth), a young engineer, share lodging behind the double gates of their compound. Leone (Mia McKenna-Bruce), Horn’s recent bride, comes to join them the same night that a man (Isaach De Bankole) appears at the fence. His name is Alboury. Like a specter in the darkness, he demands the body of his brother who died earlier that day on the site. He will hound the two men all night long until they return it, as Leone watches the disaster play out before her.

screenings.title: Wild Inside
screenings.description: Also playing: the 14-minute documentary short DREAM OF BIRDS screens with the 11:00am shows of WILD INSIDE Friday, July 31-Thursday August 6 only. Following a unique study led by Argentine physicist Gabriel Mindlin, DREAM OF BIRDS playfully explores the mystery of music through the mathematical patterns behind birdsong, and how our lives and relationships are rhythmically organized.

screenings.title: In the Glow of Darkness + Q&A
screenings.description: With the beating-heart-DIY spirit of George Kuchar and densely layered multimedia frenzy of Ryan Trecartin, L.A.-based filmmaker Tucker Bennett creates a gonzo, yet entirely plausible, sci-fi vision of our near future. In his fifth feature, Bennett melds a sincere love of ‘90s direct-to-video aesthetics and bygone blogosphere eras with a creative use of generative AI to create a kaleidoscopic, chronically-online cyberpunk-noir. With endless creativity and aesthetic integrity, Bennett lampoons and celebrates the myriad sub-cultures that populate today’s internet, betting that, in our post-ironic content-slop world, he can still stun his audience.

screenings.title: Olmo
screenings.description: Olmo just wants to be a normal teenager and hang out with his best friend, but he must help care for his bedridden father. When Olmo gets invited to a party by his beautiful neighbor, he will do whatever he can to meet up with her while embarking on an adventure of mischief, laughs, and chaos. As the night unfolds, he may come to love the very place he’s spent so long trying to escape: his home. In English and Spanish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
screenings.description: Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he’s devoted himself entirely to protecting his city — a full-time Spider-Man — but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

screenings.title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
screenings.description: Mann’s genre-defining serial-killer thriller returns in a stunning new restoration overseen by the filmmaker himself. A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a murderer and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). Adapted from the first of Thomas Harris’s Lecktor novels, MANHUNTER’s supporting cast includes Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen.

screenings.title: Hannibal
screenings.description: Hopkins reprises his role from 1991’s The Silence of the Lambs as psychiatrist-turned-cannibal serial killer Hannibal Lecter in Scott’s follow-up, a gristly fairy tale that finds FBI special agent Clarice Starling (Julianne Moore, ably taking on the role originated by Jodie Foster) racing against time to find to catch up with her old foil before he’s located by Mason R. Verger (Gary Oldman), a sadistic scion of enormous wealth who, after years earlier being grotesquely mutilated by Lecter, has dedicated the entirety of his power and influence towards a terrible and extravagant dream of vengeance. Unidentified in promotional materials and unbilled until the film’s closing credits, wholly unrecognizable under a prosthetic mask, and stripped of almost every expressive tool an actor traditionally relies upon to practice their craft, Oldman offers up an indelible portrayal of utter and absolute human corruption.

screenings.title: Club Lingerie
screenings.description: Hollywood-sleaze auteur Jared Masters is an LA based, low budget filmmaker, creating an array of women-centric features inspired by VHS slashers and 60’s B-movies. His films represent a modern take on genre films, and have John Waters/Kuchar Brothers humor to them. Jared refers to himself as a modern cult filmmaker, occasionally starring in the films he makes. The three films selected are an introduction to his filmography, highlighting his taste for camp and self-aware humor, backed by a clear love for cinema. Masters works align with the Spectacle vision to highlight underrated, seldom-viewed filmmakers and late-night summer indies.

screenings.title: Scene of the Crime
screenings.description: One of seven collaborations between Téchiné and Catherine Deneuve, Scene of the Crime is a study of domestic discontent wearing the trappings of a boilerplate thriller, its action set into motion when a disconsolate 13-year-old boy runs across a fugitive criminal (Wadeck Stanczak) while loitering in a village cemetery, an encounter that will have immense repercussions for his woebegone mother, Lili (Deneuve), her manipulative estranged husband (Victor Lanoux), and Lili’s own overbearing mother (Danielle Darrieux, César nominated for her work here.) “The crux of the film is the mother-son relationship, and it is drawn in painful accuracy… An imaginatively structured, highly cinematic experience in which we watch with detachment the workings of fate unravel with a swift yet oddly calm inevitability.” —Los Angeles Times

screenings.title: Blades of Glory
screenings.description: Two figure skating rivals are banned from the sport after a brawl over the gold medal. Joining forces, they find a loophole in the rules that allows them to skate again… as a pair!

screenings.title: Thief
screenings.description: Becoming closer to his dream of leading a normal life, a professional safecracker agrees to do a job for the mafia, who have other plans for him. Released in the US as Violent Streets, Michael Mann’s super influential minimalist neo-noir looks as authentic and original today as the day it did in 1981. Mann used real thieves as technical advisors on the film and that Tangerine Dream soundtrack is a joy. Donald Thorin’s moody and brilliant cinematography seals the deal.

screenings.title: Addams Family Values
screenings.description: Sat Aug 8: The Big Cheese Q&A w/dir. Sara Joe Wolansky & subject Adam Moskowitz, moderated by Josh Windsor, after the 7:35 sho

screenings.title: Gummo
screenings.description: Teen friends Tummler (Nick Sutton) and Solomon (Jacob Reynolds) navigate the ruins of a tiny, tornado-ravaged town in Ohio that is populated by the deformed, disturbed and perverted. When not gunning down stray cats for a few bucks, the boys pass their time getting stoned on household inhalants. Elsewhere, the mute Bunny Boy (Jacob Sewell) dons rabbit ears and is bullied by kids half his age, and sisters Dot (Chloe Sevigny) and Helen (Carisa Glucksman) dodge a pedophile.

screenings.title: Janie
screenings.description: Between the years of 1974 to 1979, not long after Manson Family trials had concluded, enigmatic artist and connoisseur of fringe culture, John Aes-Nihil, embarked on a project to “re-stage” the events leading up to the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders as a series of faux home movies, based on the legend that the Family had at one point stolen camera equipment to document their actions. The resulting feature— which, coincidentally, premiered in 1984 at EZTV alongside HIGHWAY HYPNOSIS— truly lives up to its filmmaker’s namesake Aesthetic Nihilism: Shot entirely on Super8mm and completely silent save for an accompanying soundtrack mostly comprised of music made by the Family itself (plus a little Patty Duke for good measure). The film re-frames the Manson Family story as a first-person travelogue across Southern California, imbued with chillingly realistic detail as we bear (false) witness to one of the most notorious events of the American century.

screenings.title: Ghost in the Shell
screenings.description: “We follow Kusanagi on her hunt for The Puppet Master, a hacker who can access the ‘ghosts’, or souls, of ordinary citizens and carry out cyber-crimes by proxy. Now entirely synthetic, her original human body replaced and improved on piece by piece, Kusanagi is unsure whether her ghost still lingers in her man-made form: in the opening credits, her cybernetic form is assembled in a factory, and the haunting temple chant on the soundtrack makes the process look like a religious rite.

screenings.title: Jimmy
screenings.description: Shot in dreamy 16mm black and white, Yasshadai Owens’ debut feature Jimmy offers an intimate, speculative portrait of what a young James Baldwin may have experienced during his first trip to Paris in 1948. (credit: Toronto International Film Festival)

screenings.title: The Big Cheese
screenings.description: A scrappy team of eccentric American cheesemongers defies tradition to take on the world’s top cheese masters at the Mondial du Fromage, battling cultural clashes, personal struggles, and melting cheese in pursuit of respect, redemption, and a historic victory.

screenings.title: A Child of My Own
screenings.description: This new hybrid documentary from the Oscar-nominated director of The Mole Agent and The Eternal Memory follows the shocking tale of a woman desperate for a baby. Burdened by family and societal expectations, she fakes a pregnancy and gets tangled up in a crime.

screenings.title: Good Morning
screenings.description: Two brothers in a modern Japanese suburb go on strike to bring their parents to their knees and achieve their cherished dream: owning a television set for watching sumo matches. While borrowing from his own classic I Was Born, But… (1932), Ozu turns in a decidedly contemporary, family-friendly satire of a pop-culture colonized country seen in lively Agfacolor, which also functions as the single best showcase for the master’s fondness for fart jokes.

screenings.title: Le amiche
screenings.description: Perhaps the first of Antonioni’s films to give a clear indication of the direction of his mature style, this adaptation of Cesare Pavese’s Among Women Only finds glamorous Eleonora Rossi Drago returning to her hometown of Turin to open a branch of a fashion boutique, in the process taking up with the miserable, sniping local smart set and beginning an affair with architect’s assistant Franco Fabrizi. The air of bourgeois discontentment is thick, while the disquieting train station finale is the first of Antonioni’s great set pieces.

Directed by Kent Jones (DIANE) from a witty, razor-sharp script by Samy Burch (MAY DECEMBER), LATE FAME is a funny, lively, poignant, and occasionally haunting New York story. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film 2025 96 MIN. USA MAGNOLIA PICTURES

screenings.title: White Nights
screenings.description: Italy, 1957 Directed by Luchino Visconti Based on the short story by Fyodor Dostoevsky Starring Marcello Mastroianni, Maria Schell, Jean Marais Music by Nino Rota In Italian with English subtitles Approx 103 min. “Visconti’s version of the Dostoevsky story—about the chance encounter of a couple as she is waiting in vain for her lover, and the obsessive, panic-stricken relationship which then develops between them—later filmed by Bresson as FOUR NIGHTS OF A DREAMER. Visconti traps his characters (three excellent performances) within a claustrophobic canal-side set, and the film is a series of brief walks, chases, attempted escapes, always frustrated. Shot as neo-realist high tragedy, the film offers its characters only one strange moment of escape from their night-time obsessions—a raucous, sexual, subversive scene in a dance-hall. Then the snow comes down, and with it a chilly desperation about the extent of human self-delusion.” – Time Out Restored by Luce Cinecittà, from the original 35mm negative Presented with support from the Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film A JANUS FILMS RELEASE

screenings.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: First Man
screenings.description: Dir. Damien Chazelle. 2018, 141 mins. U.S. DCP with Dolby Atmos. With Ryan Gosling, Claire Foy, Jason Clarke, Kyle Chandler, Corey Stoll, Christopher Abbott. Damien Chazelle followed up his Oscar win for La La Land with this surprising left turn, a brooding astronaut saga that plumbs genuine psychological depths in telling the life story of Neil Armstrong, the first man to walk on the moon in 1969 as part of NASA’s long-gestating Gemini program. In a kind of flip side to his portrayal of goofball loneliness in Project Hail Mary, Gosling gives one of his best performances as a family man unable to bask in the fame and success of his world-changing mission, dealing with family tragedy. Featuring stellar supporting work from Claire Foy, First Man is a sophisticated and movingly human depiction of the years leading to the Apollo 11 mission, featuring a monumental orchestral score by Justin Hurwitz and tremendous visual effects authenticity supervised by Dune’s Paul Lambert. screenings.title: Remake
screenings.description: “McElwee is a practitioner of cinema at its most elemental. He’s a man with a movie camera, pointing it at whatever or whoever is around him—which for many years included Adrian—and finding wellsprings of humor, truth, surprise... REMAKE shows him still to be a formidable artist in the face of tragedy, and one whose comically askew sensibility remains intact.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Extraordinarily clear-eyed for a work so broken-hearted: at once a home movie, an intimate diary, and an expansive study of the filmmaker’s purpose, constantly disrupting its own conclusions with expressions of anger, amusement, and still-unresolved confusion.” – Guy Lodge, Variety “Incorporation of his late son’s own footage elevates this beautiful, tragic movie from powerful to profound... Each of Ross McElwee’s deeply personal documentaries is built directly atop a fault line that separates—or connects—the microcosmic and the universal. But few films could be more unsparingly intimate than REMAKE.” – Elizabeth Weitzman, The Wrap “Emotionally piercing... meaningful and poignant.” –Warren Cantrell, The Playlist “A complex, layered contemplation of grief, memory, family ties and the meaning of filmmaking as a profoundly personal activity, REMAKE is a richly rewarding experience—emotionally, narratively and philosophically.” – Jonathan Romney, Screen International

screenings.title: A Sad and Beautiful World
screenings.description: In this sweeping love story that spans three decades of passion, heartbreak and hope, Nino and Yasmina find themselves drawn together by a magnetic relationship. As they face an impossible choice between love and survival, they must decide if they want to build a family and chart a path to happiness in Lebanon, despite the tragedies ravaging the country. In Arabic with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Center Stage
screenings.description: Hong Kong, 1991 Directed by Stanley Kwan Starring Maggie Cheung, Han Chin, Carina Lau, Tony Leung Ka-fai In Cantonese, Mandarin, and English Approx. 155 min. International superstar Maggie Cheung (IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE) embodies tragic screen siren Ruan Lingyu, known as the “Greta Garbo of China,” in this unconventional biopic by Hong Kong New Wave master Stanley Kwan (ROUGE). Praised for her moving and emotive onscreen presence, Ruan’s private life, which was frequent fodder for the vicious Shanghai tabloids, began to mirror the melodramas which brought her fame, culminating in her suicide at age 24. Kwan and Cheung paint a kaleidoscopic yet intimate portrait of the ill-fated actress, deftly blending lush period drama, archival footage, and metatextual documentary sequences of Cheung reflecting on Ruan’s legacy. The result is, much like the films of Ruan Lingyu themselves, “tender, vivid, and almost overwhelmingly moving” (Time Out). Presented by Fortune Star Media Limited, the restoration of the film was carried out from the original 35mm picture and optical soundtrack negative. The prints were repaired, cleaned and scanned in Hong Kong, then digitally restored in 4K resolution in Bologna, Italy by L'Immagine Ritrovata. Endorsed by the director, Stanley Kwan, the color correction was completed by Interface Video Production Ltd in Hong Kong. Presented with support from The Reginald S. Reinhardt, Ling-Makekau Fund for Asia-Pacific Films A FILM MOVEMENT RELEASE

screenings.title: Julian
screenings.description: Fleur and Julian fall madly in love and decide to get married in all countries where they, as two women, are allowed to do so. But after only four marriages, their journey comes to a painful and unexpected halt.

screenings.title: The Odyssey (DCP)
screenings.description: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War.

screenings.title: The Warriors
screenings.description: “Waaarriors! Come out and play-ay!” Falsely accused of responsibility for the assassination of New York’s most powerful ganglord during a citywide summit in the Bronx’s Van Cortlandt Park, Swan (Michael Beck) and his fellow Warriors now have to fight their way back, block by block and mano a mano, to the safe shores of their Coney Island turf. The film’s knuckle-busting action choreography and its vision of NYC as a coliseum-like proving grounds for epic heroism—its source, at a distance, is Xenophon’s 4th century BC Anabasis—are delectable, but its greatness lies in its attention to character, how it lets us see a crew of provincial Brooklynites gradually discovering they’re the toughest dudes in town.

screenings.title: Chocolat
screenings.description: After years of honing her craft as assistant director for the likes of Jim Jarmusch and Wim Wenders, Denis emerged as a filmmaker with a distinct and fully-formed sense of her art in this, her sensual and infinitely sensitive semi-autobiographical feature debut, drawing on memories of a childhood spent in French-occupied Africa. In Cameroon, civil servant François Cluzet comes and goes on his appointed rounds, while his young daughter and neglected wife (Giulia Boschi) gravitate ever closer to their house servant, Protée (Isaach de Bankolé) in his absence, and the murmurs of anti-colonial resistance increase in vehemence away from eavesdropping whites. “Some kind of miniature classic.”—Vincent Canby, The New York Times

screenings.title: The Piano - New 4K Restoration
screenings.description: Ada – mute since birth – her nine year old daughter and her piano arrive to an arranged marriage in the remote bush of nineteenth century New Zealand. Of all her belongings her husband refuses to transport the piano and it is left behind on the beach. Unable to bear its certain destruction, Ada strikes a bargain with an illiterate tattooed neighbour. She may earn her piano back if she allows him to do certain things while she plays ; one black key for every lesson. The arrangement draws all three deeper and deeper into a complex emotional, sexual bond remarkable for its naive passion and frightening disregard for limits.

screenings.title: ∞ Infinity Day: Parallel Universes Explained!
screenings.description: Quantum mechanics explore how a particle can be superimposed into multiple states of being at the same time. When disturbed by observation or measurement, particles “choose” from one of many possible states and present just one. What are the implications of this choice? Its study is one of the foundations of the theory in physics underpinning exploration of parallel universes. Prepare to have your worldview expanded in this conversation led by quantum physicist Niccolo Bigagli, exploring the scientific underpinning of the multiverse, illustrated by favorite film clips. RSVP recommended. Seating is first come, first served. Special guests Niccolo Bigagli is a quantum physicist whose experiments span the study of quantum particles from their most fundamental properties as single entities to their behavior when many thousands are brought together. In his PhD, Niccolò observed for the first time a novel phase of matter, a Bose Einstein Condensate of dipolar molecules, where molecules act as a fascinating single body while still interacting amongst themselves. Currently, he is studying quantum networks, that is how to harness photons’ quantum mechanical nature to unlock new technology and new experimental capabilities. Niccolò also dabbles in film and photography, with a special interest in analog techniques. screenings.title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World
screenings.description: If poetry had a pop icon, Mary Oliver would be it. Celebrated bestseller, Pulitzer Prize winner, lover of dogs and long walks in the woods, openly queer but intensely private, Oliver was America’s unlikely contemporary mystic, stalking the ponds and forests of Cape Cod for nearly 50 years in order to open herself – and her readers – to the known and unknowable world. From a lonely childhood to literary fame, Oliver’s life was shaped by devotion to nature, paying attention, and the long journey toward learning to love and to be loved. Her poems inspire liberals and conservatives, atheists and believers, naturalists and urbanites, speaking directly to contemporary anxieties about attention, presence, and the human relationship with the natural world – issues that feel especially pressing in an era of climate crisis, digital distraction, and social fragmentation.

screenings.title: Olmo

As the night unfolds, he may come to love the very place he’s spent so long trying to escape: his home. In English and Spanish with English subtitles.

screenings.title: The Samurai and the Prisoner
screenings.description: When Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki) rises up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Masaki Suda), he finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle. Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Michael Mann's Manhunter: The Final Cut
screenings.description: Mann’s genre-defining serial-killer thriller returns in a stunning new restoration overseen by the filmmaker himself. A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a murderer and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). Adapted from the first of Thomas Harris’s Lecktor novels, MANHUNTER’s supporting cast includes Tom Noonan as the hunted killer, and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen.

screenings.title: The Chaser
screenings.description: Drawing inspiration from the gristly exploits of South Korean serial killer Yoo Young-chul, Na’s astonishingly assured directorial debut stars Ha Jung-woo as a sadistic killer, Ji Yeong-min, and Kim Yoon-seok as Joong-ho, an ex-detective with a checkered past now running a prostitution ring. After helplessly watching his stable of employees disappear and dwindle, Joong-ho sets out to find the sicko responsible—and in the course of a sleepless night of cat and mouse, finds he has to contend not only with the killer’s calculating intelligence and red herring misleads, but with an incompetent police force and a thicket of bureaucratic barriers that seem to have been erected with the specific purpose of allowing the guilty to get away clean. Winner of Best Actor, Best Film, and Best Director at Korea’s Grand Bell Awards, The Chaser is both a precision-tuned white-knuckle thriller and an agonized exploration of insoluble moral conundrums.

screenings.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1968, 149 mins (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood. As brilliantly engineered as the space program itself, Stanley Kubrick’s mysterious and profound sci-fi epic—“the ultimate trip”—is about nothing less than the beauty and the banality of civilization, blending cool satire, an elaborate vision of the future, and passages of avant-garde cinematic inventiveness. Set in a future that is already the past, 2001 envisions space travel as both hilariously routine and mind-bending, a journey to the infinite and beyond that forever changed the way we see the universe and cinema itself. As experienced on 70mm in MoMI’s Redstone Theater, Kubrick’s surreal masterwork still has the ability to conduct viewers to untold, unknowable realms of artistry and daring.
