screenings.title: Raw
screenings.description: Justine (Garance Marillier), a lifelong vegetarian, has just started attending the same Belgian veterinary school that her older sister Alexia (Ella Rumpf) goes to, and after she’s forced to eat a raw rabbit kidney during a hazing ritual, she suddenly finds herself experiencing carnivorous cravings that her sibling understands all too well. Winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Cannes Film Festival, Ducournau’s gruesome drama of sexual awakening and campus cannibalism found its way onto a great many best-of-the-year lists, and announced the appearance of a new virtuoso of body horror.

screenings.title: House
screenings.description: A demonic house cat is only one of the cast of outlandish characters in Ôbayashi’s psychedelic ghost story in which a schoolgirl and six of her teen classmates go on a trip to her ailing aunt’s mist-wreathed country house and find themselves caught up a whirlpool of lo-fi nightmare visions and supernatural menaces with a taste for young flesh. Animated household appliances, airborne severed heads, and a ravenous piano are among the trials the girls face in this delirious (and hilarious) cult phenom.

screenings.title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Bugs We Love(?)
screenings.description: Stathes joins Metrograph in August with Bugs We Love(?), a selection of vintage animated shorts dedicated to the true stars of summertime—insects! Come enjoy a crabby farmer’'s run-in with a number of pesky mosquitoes, a chivalrous fly saving his mate from an enemy species, a musical beetle conducting a swing band, a famous sailor battling termites in his home, a canine’s hilarious showdown with his own parasitic flea, and other amusing tales. Spanning the 1920s through the ’50s, this assortment showcases classic characters such as Elmer Fudd, Popeye, Felix the Cat, Porky Pig, and more.

screenings.title: Days and Nights in the Forest
screenings.description: Leaving crowded Calcutta behind for a few days of rustication in the Palamau woods—while bringing the deeply ingrained prejudices of their castes and their sex along as baggage—four middle-class young men hope that their holiday will provide the opportunity for a passing romantic fling, but instead find themselves presented with the mortifying prospect of having to confront their own boorish biases. “Modern and novelistic. Ray [works] in terrain perhaps more familiar to Cassavetes… Selfish men and their hopes and cruelties and spectacular lack of wisdom. Women who see through them. The great Soumitra Chatterjee: lost but searching. The great Sharmila Tagore: mysterious, cerebral, mesmerizing. From the master, another masterpiece.” —Wes Anderson

screenings.title: Hamlet (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Kenneth Branagh. 1996, 238 mins. 70mm with intermission. With Kenneth Branagh, Kate Winslet, Julie Christie, Michael Maloney, Derek Jacobi, Richard Briers, Judi Dench, Gérard Depardieu, Richard Attenborough, Brian Blessed, Billy Crystal, Robin Wiliams, John Gielgud, Rufus Sewell, Timothy Spall, Charlton Heston. Though it’s one of the most frequently adapted works in the history of cinema, William Shakespeare’s Hamlet had never been filmed in its complete unabridged version—until Kenneth Branagh went about the task for this lavish, star-studded 1996 production. Set within the vast, cold interiors of a vaguely 19th-century manor, this magnificent adaptation stars Branagh as the melancholy son of the Danish court, along with a Who’s Who of late 20th-century master thespians, including Christie, Jacobi, Dench, Depardieu, Gielgud, and a young Winslet as the aggrieved Ophelia, all captured in sumptuous 70mm. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership.

screenings.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
screenings.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage.

screenings.title: Spider Baby
screenings.description: Chauffeur Lon Chaney, Jr. attempts to cover up the homicidal and cannibalistic indiscretions of his charges, the feral Merrye family—a trio of variously degenerate long-orphaned siblings played by Jill Banner, Beverly Washburn, and Sid Haig—as distant relations try to sell their decaying home out from under them in this drive-in horror melodrama, a work of guffaw-worthy gallows humor and genuine pathos. There’s more than a touch of Southern-fried Gothic in the mix here, with writer-director Hill maintaining a tricky balance of tragedy and farce and has a gas playing with classic hereditary curse tropes, while his ensemble cast provide gleefully going-for-broke performances that start at over-the-top and only go further up from there.

screenings.title: The Jungle Book
screenings.description: Inspired by the adventures of the foundling Mowgli in Rudyard Kipling’s 1894 collection of the same name, The Jungle Book—the final animated Disney feature to be overseen in its production by Uncle Walt—would become one of the studio’s biggest hits, thanks in no small part to its exceptional confluence of vocal talent (yes, that’s George Sanders as the suavely sinister Bengal tiger Shere Khan) and unforgettable songbook, including perennial favorites “The Bare Necessities” and “I Wanna Be Like You (The Monkey Song),” the latter volcanically belted out by none other than jump blues howler extraordinaire Louis Prima. Brisk, breezy, and simply buckets of fun.

screenings.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
screenings.description: A world-conquering pop culture phenomenon on its original release, today it’s easier to see Spielberg’s boy-and-his-alien fable as the movie it always was—modest and familiar in its domestic setting, supremely sensitive to all the fun and the fear of childhood, and very often close to achieving the sublime. Abandoned on earth, a duck-walking alien longing to “Phone home” encounters a human boy who needs companionship, with unforgettable and heart-rending results.

screenings.title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
screenings.description: Dir. Jacques Demy. 1964, 92 mins. France. DCP. With Catherine Deneuve, Nino Castelnuovo, Marc Michel, Anne Vernon. One of the most exquisite romances ever filmed, Jacques Demy’s gorgeous, melancholy tale of young love thwarted by harsh reality is completely sung through to an unforgettable score by the great Michel Legrand. Deneuve commands the screen as the daughter of an umbrella-shop owner who falls hard for a sweet-faced young car mechanic, who is eventually sent off to fight in the Algerian War. Perhaps the tenderest film of the French New Wave, Demy’s lovely operetta is a triumph of cinematography, costume design, art direction, and music. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / free for MoMI members at the Senior/Student level and above. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. screenings.title: The Dark Knight
screenings.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.”

screenings.title: Petite Maman
screenings.description: Sciamma’s follow-up to her lauded Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a tender, compassionate, and refreshingly unsentimental study of loss as experienced by a child; a lovely and effervescent work centered on eight-year-old Nelly (Joséphine Sanz) who, when wandering in the woods shortly after the death of her beloved grandmother, encounters an awfully familiar-looking girl (Gabrielle Sanz, Joséphine’s twin sister) who offers Nelly a most unexpected chance to grow closer to both her mother and late grandmother. “Luminous… With delicacy, minimal dialogue, and lucid, harmoniously balanced images, Sciamma invites you into a world that is by turns ordinary and enigmatic.” —Manohla Dargis, The New York Times

screenings.description: Dir. David Lean. 1962, 227 mins. (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Peter O’Toole, Omar Sharif, Alec Guinness, Anthony Quinn. The apex of David Lean’s magnificent career was this unparalleled spectacle which won seven Oscars, including Best Picture. Lawrence of Arabia rocketed Peter O’Toole to stardom as real-life adventurer T. E. Lawrence, a former British officer whose expedition to Cairo in 1916 leads him to side with the Arabs against the Turks, eventually organizing his own guerrilla army. With its overwhelming widescreen desert vistas, this is one of cinema’s most transporting experiences, a film that all but demands the big-screen treatment. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Please note: Both of these screenings are sold out. Standby tickets may become available at the door on the evening of the event.

screenings.title: Withnail and I
screenings.description: Based loosely on writer/director Robinson’s memories of being a penniless actor in late ’60s London, Withnail and I stars Richard E. Grant and Paul McGann as two unemployed thesps and Camden Town flatmates—hard-drinking, dissolute Withnail and an unnamed “I,” respectively—who “go on holiday by mistake” at the Lake District home of Withnail’s pompous Uncle Monty (Richard Griffiths), and there commence a program of boozing, bickering, and baiting. Endlessly quotable (“We want the finest wines available to humanity. And we want them here, and we want them now!”), winningly splenetic and shambolic and, taken altogether, about as enjoyable a film of pills, thrills, and bellyaches as you’ll ever find.

screenings.title: Pastorale
screenings.description: A Tbilisi-based string quartet, seeking a quiet place to practice, light out for a mountain village, taking lodgings with the family of a long-haul truck driver and rehearsing on the house’s veranda as, around them, the daily life of the mountain hamlet continues unabated, albeit to an incongruous soundtrack of classical music. The film that marks Iosseliani’s decisive turn towards tales in which a community—or, at any rate, an ensemble—act as protagonist, Pastorale, winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival, is a work of marvelously polished little moments, not another stereotyped city mouse-country mouse culture-clash but something far more elusive, more insightful, and ultimately more affecting.

screenings.description: In the French countryside, in a chateau that’s arrived at a state of genteel decay, two eccentric old women live, as they have for years, practicing the nearly forgotten rituals of the prewar haute bourgeoisie, surrounded by beautiful, dusty relics of a bygone era—a stasis soon to be interrupted by a funeral and the arrival of two heirs eager to turn the property into a profit. An intricate network narrative, like Iosseliani’s Pastorale or Favorites of the Moon, Chasing Butterflies is as much about a way of life—or, more accurately, ways of life—as it is about individuals, an elegiac but clear-eyed depiction of a faded, wilting tradition, absurd and touching, about to be blown away by the stiff winds of contemporary capitalism.

screenings.title: 54: The Director's Cut + Q&A | This is Cinématographe
screenings.description: New York City, 1979: working class Jersey City teenager Shane (Ryan Phillippe, Cruel Intentions) becomes infatuated with Studio 54, a lavish Manhattan nightclub known for decadence. Shane’s time at 54 introduces him to a cast of characters including real life nightclub owner Steve Rubell (Mike Myers, Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery), busboy Greg (Breckin Meyer, Clueless), coat checker Anita (Salma Hayek, Traffic), and actress Julie (Neve Campbell, Scream).

screenings.title: After Hours
screenings.description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today.

screenings.title: Taste of Streep presents: Mamma Mia!
The Wind that Shakes the Barley | 2006 Movies

screenings.title: Taste of Streep: Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again
Maddie's Secret
screenings.description: Maddie’s Secret is comedian, writer, and actor John Early’s critically acclaimed directorial debut starring himself as Maddie, a plucky dishwasher who leaps to viral superstardom at a trendy food content creation company. While her life seems picturesque — complete with an adoring husband (Eric Rahill), ride-or-die best friend (Kate Berlant) and a cupboard full of woman-owned ethically-sourced chili crisp to boot — mounting professional pressures threaten to reawaken a hidden secret from her troubled past. A pitch-perfect blend of satire, melodrama, daring tonal shifts and intimate performances, the film marks a bold new voice in contemporary cinema.

screenings.title: Taste of Streep presents: Mamma Mia!
When We Saw Each Other More Often + Q&A
screenings.description: Flora leaves. Antonis gets left behind. Elit moves in. Benni and Caro can’t seem to move on. In the classrooms, cafés, bars and train stations of an unnamed German city, the lives of several young people intersect.

screenings.title: Chinatown
screenings.description: Widely regarded as one of the greatest American films ever made, this classic neo-noir from director Roman Polanski features an Oscar-winning screenplay by Robert Towne and stars Jack Nicholson as a private investigator, whose seemingly routine adultery case unravels into a labyrinth of murder, political corruption, and family secrets in 1930s Los Angeles. Huston stars as Noah Cross, a charismatic patriarch whose immense wealth and influence conceal a monstrous moral rot. Adding an intriguing off-screen connection, Nicholson was romantically involved with Huston’s daughter, Anjelica Huston, during the production, beginning a relationship that would last for many years.

screenings.title: Taste of Streep presents: Mamma Mia!
The Black Dahlia | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: Two cops in the 1940s Los Angeles investigate the murder of a Hollywood starlet (Mia Kirshner), and one (Aaron Eckhart) puts his marriage in jeopardy by obsessing over the crime, while the other (Josh Hartnett) becomes involved with a woman (Hilary Swank) from a prominent family, who happens to have an unsavory tie to the victim.

screenings.title: In the Family + Q&A
screenings.description: In the town of Martin, Tennessee, Chip Hines, a precocious six year old, has only known life with his two dads, Cody and Joey. And a good life it is. When Cody dies suddenly in a car accident, Joey and Chip struggle to find their footing again. Just as they begin to, Cody’s will reveals that he named his sister as Chip’s guardian. The years of Joey’s acceptance into the family unravel as Chip is taken away from him. In his now solitary home life, Joey searches for a solution. The law is not on his side, but friends are. Armed with their comfort and inspired by memories of Cody, Joey finds a path to peace with the family and closer to his son.

screenings.title: Come What May
screenings.description: Come What May is an intimate, unflinching portrait of beloved comedian Ralphie May, whose large personality and even larger size set him apart from the rest and helped skyrocket him to fame. This loving husband and father fell victim to enablers, addiction, and abuse, causing his bright light to burn out far too quickly. Featuring candid interviews with friends and family, alongside never-before-seen archival footage, what unfolds is a loving tribute to a flawed and complicated man who brought joy to millions, but pain and heartbreak to those who knew him best.

screenings.title: The Dark Knight
screenings.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.”

screenings.title: Days and Nights in the Forest
screenings.description: Leaving crowded Calcutta behind for a few days of rustication in the Palamau woods—while bringing the deeply ingrained prejudices of their castes and their sex along as baggage—four middle-class young men hope that their holiday will provide the opportunity for a passing romantic fling, but instead find themselves presented with the mortifying prospect of having to confront their own boorish biases. “Modern and novelistic. Ray [works] in terrain perhaps more familiar to Cassavetes… Selfish men and their hopes and cruelties and spectacular lack of wisdom. Women who see through them. The great Soumitra Chatterjee: lost but searching. The great Sharmila Tagore: mysterious, cerebral, mesmerizing. From the master, another masterpiece.” —Wes Anderson

screenings.title: Her Private Hell
screenings.description: When a mysterious mist engulfs a futuristic metropolis, unleashing a deadly and elusive entity, a troubled young woman searches for her father. Her quest collides with an American GI on a harrowing odyssey to rescue his daughter from Hell.

screenings.title: Jennifer's Body
screenings.description: High school besties Anita and Jennifer (Amanda Seyfried and Megan Fox) are all but inseparable—though “Needy” Anita is a mousy bookworm and Jennifer a lusted-after member of the color guard—but can their opposites-attract dynamic survive Jennifer’s transformation into a succubus with an insatiable appetite for the flesh of their male classmates? A celebration of the pleasures of camp, kink, and practical gore effects that moves at sleek screwball feed thanks to Diablo Cody’s rat-a-tat screenplay, Kusama’s brisk direction, and the on-a-dime comic timing of its leads. (Not to speak of the redoubtable Amy Sedaris, as Anita’s perpetually disheveled, out-to-lunch mother.)

screenings.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
screenings.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage.

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1968, 149 mins (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood. As brilliantly engineered as the space program itself, Stanley Kubrick’s mysterious and profound sci-fi epic—“the ultimate trip”—is about nothing less than the beauty and the banality of civilization, blending cool satire, an elaborate vision of the future, and passages of avant-garde cinematic inventiveness. Set in a future that is already the past, 2001 envisions space travel as both hilariously routine and mind-bending, a journey to the infinite and beyond that forever changed the way we see the universe and cinema itself. As experienced on 70mm in MoMI’s Redstone Theater, Kubrick’s surreal masterwork still has the ability to conduct viewers to untold, unknowable realms of artistry and daring. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. screenings.title: Eve's Bayou
screenings.description: One of the essential works of the 1990s and recently selected for the Library of Congress’ National Film Registry, Eve’s Bayou is a film of rich, steamy sexuality and an incredible sense of place, that follows the loss of innocence that occurs when the daughter of a well-to-do Louisiana family (Jurnee Smollett) catches her father (Samuel L. Jackson) in a moment of infidelity. Boasting an impressive line-up of actresses, including living legends Lynne Whitfield, Debbi Morgan, Meagan Good, and Carroll, unforgettably intense as the mysterious fortune teller Elzora, it’s a seductive tour de force in an atmosphere thick with voodoo, other Creole legends, and household magic.

screenings.title: Der Fan
screenings.description: Teen runaway Simone (Désirée Nosbusch, entrancingly opaque) loves the Neue Deutsche Welle pop singer known only as “R” (Bodo Staiger)… loves him so much, in fact, that she could just about eat him alive. And when she finally meets her idol—only to be callously treated by him as a disposable sex object—well, Simone gets the chance to really become one with her beloved forever. A hard, cool-to-the-touch, and utterly riveting slow-burn psychological thriller that, newly restored for its first ever US theatrical release, speaks to our age of parasocial obsession, featuring a sinister synth-pop soundtrack by Staiger’s own band, Rheingold, and a last act that’s finger-lickin’ good.

screenings.title: I Want Your Sex
screenings.description: In the latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Araki (“Mysterious Skin”), I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twenty-something whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli xcx) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery and murder through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is known.
screenings.country: I Want Your Sex Romance, Thriller

screenings.title: House
screenings.description: A demonic house cat is only one of the cast of outlandish characters in Ôbayashi’s psychedelic ghost story in which a schoolgirl and six of her teen classmates go on a trip to her ailing aunt’s mist-wreathed country house and find themselves caught up a whirlpool of lo-fi nightmare visions and supernatural menaces with a taste for young flesh. Animated household appliances, airborne severed heads, and a ravenous piano are among the trials the girls face in this delirious (and hilarious) cult phenom.

screenings.title: Raw
screenings.description: Justine (Garance Marillier), a lifelong vegetarian, has just started attending the same Belgian veterinary school that her older sister Alexia (Ella Rumpf) goes to, and after she’s forced to eat a raw rabbit kidney during a hazing ritual, she suddenly finds herself experiencing carnivorous cravings that her sibling understands all too well. Winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Cannes Film Festival, Ducournau’s gruesome drama of sexual awakening and campus cannibalism found its way onto a great many best-of-the-year lists, and announced the appearance of a new virtuoso of body horror.

screenings.title: Old Joy
screenings.description: Two boyhood pals who have since drifted apart, played by Daniel London and musician Will Oldham, impulsively reunite for a camping and hiking trip in the verdant woods of the Pacific Northwest in Reichardt’s breakout sophomore feature, released 12 years after debut River of Grass. Dialogue is at a minimum in Reichardt’s serene, solemn film, but London and Oldham’s taciturn, intricately detailed performances—as well as the plangent score by Yo La Tengo and the evocative photographing of the landscape—speak volumes about middle-aged mournfulness and faded friendship. Distributor: Janus Films

screenings.title: Petite Maman
screenings.description: Sciamma’s follow-up to her lauded Portrait of a Lady on Fire is a tender, compassionate, and refreshingly unsentimental study of loss as experienced by a child; a lovely and effervescent work centered on eight-year-old Nelly (Joséphine Sanz) who, when wandering in the woods shortly after the death of her beloved grandmother, encounters an awfully familiar-looking girl (Gabrielle Sanz, Joséphine’s twin sister) who offers Nelly a most unexpected chance to grow closer to both her mother and late grandmother. “Luminous… With delicacy, minimal dialogue, and lucid, harmoniously balanced images, Sciamma invites you into a world that is by turns ordinary and enigmatic.” —Manohla Dargis, The New York Times

screenings.title: Pacific Rim
screenings.description: Dir. Guillermo Del Toro. 2013, 131 mins. U.S. DCP with Dolby Atmos. With Idris Elba, Charlie Hunnam, Rinko Kikuchi, Charlie Day, Ron Perlman. Guillermo Del Toro’s gargantuan spectacle is his own variation on the kaiju film, concerning a battle royale between mankind and a race of deadly giant sea creatures that have entered the human realm via an interdimensional portal at the bottom of the Pacific Ocean. The only way to combat the mammoth foes is for us to create huge mecha-humanoids and send them into battle. Dedicated to such artists as stop motion master Ray Harryhausen and Godzilla creator Ishiro Honda, Del Toro’s film is one of the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s most good-natured, purely entertaining extravaganzas. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / discounted for MoMI members ($7–$11). There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Mississippi Mermaid
screenings.description: “St. Laurent and Deneuve’s third collaboration in 1969 has the star dressed to kill. Taking place partly on the island of Réunion, the film was the perfect vessel to highlight the designer’s vision for his 1968 Spring/Summer Rive Gauche collection, which drew heavily from safari and military dress aesthetics. Truffaut said of St. Laurent: ‘Of all the major couturiers, he is the biggest cinephile; he understood what film costumes were supposed to be and was able to conceive them in a way that could be adapted to different movements and styles.’” —David Campany, Creative Director, International Center of Photography

screenings.title: Chungking Express
screenings.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking.

screenings.title: The Untouchables
screenings.description: Dir. Brian De Palma. 1987, 119 mins. 70mm. With Kevin Costner, Sean Connery, Charles Martin Smith, Andy García, Robert De Niro. Master craftsman De Palma collaborated with playwright David Mamet to adapt the 1950s ABC television series—itself an adaptation of Elliot Ness’s autobiography—into one of the great cinematic achievements of the 1980s. In the performance that helped launch him to stardom, Costner plays Ness, a lawman in Prohibition-era Chicago tracking notorious criminal kingpin Al Capone (De Niro), whose net of influence over the city extends to officers in Ness’s own department. He teams with a fearless veteran Irish cop (Connery, in an Oscar-winning performance) and principled Italian American rookie (Garcia) to pursue justice in the face of overwhelming criminality and corruption. Never one to shy away from a challenge, De Palma shoots the hell out of The Untouchables, assisting universally strong performances with majestic framing, virtuosic movement, and undaunted violence. And yes, during an elaborate showdown in Chicago’s Union Station, he directly apes the Odessa Steps sequence from Eisenstein’s Potemkin—one of the best-known scenes in the history of cinema—not as a winking homage, but with the confidence that he can exceed it. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Stand By Me
screenings.description: Adapting King’s novella The Body, Reiner created this rightly beloved, clear-eyed evocation of 1950s America, starring River Phoenix, Wil Wheaton, Corey Feldman, and Jerry O’Connell as a group of adolescent friends in small-town Oregon who set out to find a missing boy believed to be dead, along the way facing a leech-infested swimming hole, a bullying Kiefer Sutherland, and the end of innocence.

screenings.title: In My Skin
screenings.description: De Van writes, directs, and stars in this morbidly transfixing, at times suffocatingly intimate psychodrama from the high heady horrifying heyday of New French Extremity, playing Ester, a seemingly well adjusted Parisian career woman whose life changes dramatically after a chance injury to her leg one night sends her into a spiraling obsession with her body, in all of its frailty and friability, one that in time will become, in more than one sense, self-consuming. “As unrelenting an exploration of isolation and dissociation as Roman Polanski’s Repulsion… [A] remarkable debut film.” —The New York Times

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong Li), acting as distractions now that his true love, Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung, seen in flashback), has disappeared. Intercutting scenes from Chow’s footloose life—several of these taking place on subsequent Christmas Eves—with scenes from his novel-in-progress, set in the titular year, it’s a film of voluptuous melancholy.

screenings.title: Lady in the Water
screenings.description: To its detractors, evidence of auteur egomania run amok, to its admirers, among the most personal and individualistic studio productions of the last 20 years, Lady in the Water is a daring admixture of the quotidian and the fantastic, in which the superintendent of a Philadelphia apartment complex (Paul Giamatti), on discovering a young woman of unknown origins (Bryce Dallas Howard) floating in the pool of the building he manages, unwittingly finds himself a character in an unfolding fairy tale. Key to Shyamalan’s singular tonal balance here is Christopher Doyle’s lushly atmospheric camerawork; who else, one wonders, could make a block of drab row houses in the City of Brotherly Love feel like a Pre-Raphaelite canvas?

screenings.title: Frances Ha
screenings.description: Dir. Noah Baumbach. 2013, 86 mins. U.S. DCP. With Greta Gerwig, Mickey Sumner, Adam Driver, Michael Zegen, Charlotte D’Ambroise, Grace Gummer. With its lustrous black-and-white cinematography, clever and moving script by Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach, and vibrant central performance by Gerwig as the eponymous Frances, this lovely pocket portrait of an “undatable” young woman navigating early twenty-first century New York friendships, relationships, post-college malaise, and exorbitant ATM fees has already proven to be a generational cornerstone. Endlessly rewatchable, Frances Ha moves with the fleet-footed lightness and knowing of a French New Wave classic yet with a tenderness and empathy that feels tuned into the specific experiences of living in a city that’s both unforgiving and undeniable. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / free for MoMI members at the Senior/Student level and above. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Nenette and Boni
screenings.description: Alice Houri and Grégoire Colin, playing an estranged sister and brother reunited after leaving the same broken home behind, are the title characters of Denis’s domestic drama, a film whose emotional generosity is perfectly matched by the luminous warmth of its images. Nénette, 15 and pregnant, shows up on the doorstep of her brother, a terminally horny 19-year-old line cook at a Marseilles pizzeria, and after initial misgivings, the siblings clumsily try their hand at forming a family. Denis’s first collaboration with the Nottingham group Tindersticks, who would go on to join Jean-Louis Ughetto in the director’s repertory ensemble of professional associates, both parties contributing inestimably to the film’s marvelous, buoyant musicality—as does Brian Wilson, as the Beach Boys’ “God Only Knows” gets an indelible needle drop.

screenings.title: City Dudes
screenings.description: City Dudes is the monthly “blindfolded” screening series at the Roxy Cinema New York curated and hosted by the American cinematographer Sean Price Williams and the American writer Nick Pinkerton. Might could be they’ll have the occasional Exciting Guest on-hand as well!

screenings.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show: Live Shadow Cast
screenings.description: Starring Tim Curry Susan Sarandon Barry Bostwick Richard O'Brien Patricia Quinn Little Nell Meat Loaf

screenings.title: Mulholland Drive [35mm]
screenings.description: Beginning its life as an aborted TV pilot concerning blonde aspiring actress Betty Elms (Naomi Watts, transcendent) and an amnesiac brunette (Laura Harring) who stumbles into her, Mulholland Dr. would be reborn as a strange, sorrowful, and maddeningly mysterious film noir-inflected feature, following the duo on a sleuthing journey that leads them through Hollywood, to the enigmatic night club Silencio, and a series of unnerving incidents and transformations. Heartbreaking, hilarious, and terrifying by turns, and always on the razor’s edge of the inexplicable.

screenings.title: True Romance
screenings.description: Comic shop clerk, Elvis aficionado, and repository of cult movie esoterica, Slater’s Clarence Worley goes from nerd to knight errant after his whirlwind romance with call girl Alabama (Patricia Arquette), taking her on the lam after he forcefully retires her pimp (Gary Oldman) and finds himself holding a huge stash of contraband cocaine. A bloody valentine from screenwriter Quentin Tarantino, with a gallery of supporting players including Dennis Hopper, Brad Pitt, and Christopher Walken handling his delectable free-verse pulp poetry. Distributor: Swank Motion Pictures

screenings.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
screenings.description: A world-conquering pop culture phenomenon on its original release, today it’s easier to see Spielberg’s boy-and-his-alien fable as the movie it always was—modest and familiar in its domestic setting, supremely sensitive to all the fun and the fear of childhood, and very often close to achieving the sublime. Abandoned on earth, a duck-walking alien longing to “Phone home” encounters a human boy who needs companionship, with unforgettable and heart-rending results.

screenings.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
screenings.description: The Fu-Ho Grand, a movie palace in Taipei, is closing its doors. Its valedictory screening: King Hu’s 1967 wuxia epic Dragon Inn, playing to a motley smattering of spectators, including two stars of Hu’s original opus, Miao Tien and Shih Chun, watching their younger selves with tears in their eyes.

screenings.title: It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kramer. 1963, 180 mins. plus intermission. 70mm. With Spencer Tracy, Edie Adams, Milton Berle, Ethel Merman. This beloved, epic Hollywood comedy is a three-hour-plus extravaganza of slapstick excess that lets loose an unparalleled cast of legends—including Milton Berle, Sid Caesar, Buddy Hackett, Ethel Merman, Mickey Rooney, Dick Shawn, Spencer Tracy, and Jonathan Winters (just for starters)—in a wild plot about a hunt for buried treasure. With its super-wide frame, jam-packed with gags big and small, Stanley Kramer’s classic is endless juvenile fun that has retained an intense fan following. Please note that the film will be shown with a 20-minute intermission that will include police-call audio. Tickets: $25 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership.

screenings.title: Lady in the Water
screenings.description: To its detractors, evidence of auteur egomania run amok, to its admirers, among the most personal and individualistic studio productions of the last 20 years, Lady in the Water is a daring admixture of the quotidian and the fantastic, in which the superintendent of a Philadelphia apartment complex (Paul Giamatti), on discovering a young woman of unknown origins (Bryce Dallas Howard) floating in the pool of the building he manages, unwittingly finds himself a character in an unfolding fairy tale. Key to Shyamalan’s singular tonal balance here is Christopher Doyle’s lushly atmospheric camerawork; who else, one wonders, could make a block of drab row houses in the City of Brotherly Love feel like a Pre-Raphaelite canvas?

screenings.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
screenings.description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent production which returns to the original Stoker text and draws out the piercing sexual ache and romantic longing implicit therein.

screenings.title: A. Rimbaud
screenings.description: The improbable life of French poet Arthur Rimbaud unfolds with all the shock and playfulness of his poetry.

screenings.title: Der Fan
screenings.description: Teen runaway Simone (Désirée Nosbusch, entrancingly opaque) loves the Neue Deutsche Welle pop singer known only as “R” (Bodo Staiger)… loves him so much, in fact, that she could just about eat him alive. And when she finally meets her idol—only to be callously treated by him as a disposable sex object—well, Simone gets the chance to really become one with her beloved forever. A hard, cool-to-the-touch, and utterly riveting slow-burn psychological thriller that, newly restored for its first ever US theatrical release, speaks to our age of parasocial obsession, featuring a sinister synth-pop soundtrack by Staiger’s own band, Rheingold, and a last act that’s finger-lickin’ good.

screenings.title: Mulholland Drive [35mm]
screenings.description: Beginning its life as an aborted TV pilot concerning blonde aspiring actress Betty Elms (Naomi Watts, transcendent) and an amnesiac brunette (Laura Harring) who stumbles into her, Mulholland Dr. would be reborn as a strange, sorrowful, and maddeningly mysterious film noir-inflected feature, following the duo on a sleuthing journey that leads them through Hollywood, to the enigmatic night club Silencio, and a series of unnerving incidents and transformations. Heartbreaking, hilarious, and terrifying by turns, and always on the razor’s edge of the inexplicable.

screenings.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1968, 149 mins (plus intermission). U.S. 70mm. With Keir Dullea, Gary Lockwood. As brilliantly engineered as the space program itself, Stanley Kubrick’s mysterious and profound sci-fi epic—“the ultimate trip”—is about nothing less than the beauty and the banality of civilization, blending cool satire, an elaborate vision of the future, and passages of avant-garde cinematic inventiveness. Set in a future that is already the past, 2001 envisions space travel as both hilariously routine and mind-bending, a journey to the infinite and beyond that forever changed the way we see the universe and cinema itself. As experienced on 70mm in MoMI’s Redstone Theater, Kubrick’s surreal masterwork still has the ability to conduct viewers to untold, unknowable realms of artistry and daring. screenings.title: When We Saw Each Other More Often + Q&A
screenings.description: Flora leaves. Antonis gets left behind. Elit moves in. Benni and Caro can’t seem to move on. In the classrooms, cafés, bars and train stations of an unnamed German city, the lives of several young people intersect.

screenings.title: Eve's Bayou
screenings.description: One of the essential works of the 1990s and recently selected for the Library of Congress’ National Film Registry, Eve’s Bayou is a film of rich, steamy sexuality and an incredible sense of place, that follows the loss of innocence that occurs when the daughter of a well-to-do Louisiana family (Jurnee Smollett) catches her father (Samuel L. Jackson) in a moment of infidelity. Boasting an impressive line-up of actresses, including living legends Lynne Whitfield, Debbi Morgan, Meagan Good, and Carroll, unforgettably intense as the mysterious fortune teller Elzora, it’s a seductive tour de force in an atmosphere thick with voodoo, other Creole legends, and household magic.

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong Li), acting as distractions now that his true love, Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung, seen in flashback), has disappeared. Intercutting scenes from Chow’s footloose life—several of these taking place on subsequent Christmas Eves—with scenes from his novel-in-progress, set in the titular year, it’s a film of voluptuous melancholy.

screenings.title: Jennifer's Body
screenings.description: High school besties Anita and Jennifer (Amanda Seyfried and Megan Fox) are all but inseparable—though “Needy” Anita is a mousy bookworm and Jennifer a lusted-after member of the color guard—but can their opposites-attract dynamic survive Jennifer’s transformation into a succubus with an insatiable appetite for the flesh of their male classmates? A celebration of the pleasures of camp, kink, and practical gore effects that moves at sleek screwball feed thanks to Diablo Cody’s rat-a-tat screenplay, Kusama’s brisk direction, and the on-a-dime comic timing of its leads. (Not to speak of the redoubtable Amy Sedaris, as Anita’s perpetually disheveled, out-to-lunch mother.)

screenings.title: I Want Your Sex
screenings.description: In the latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Araki (“Mysterious Skin”), I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twenty-something whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli xcx) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery and murder through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is known.

After Hours
screenings.description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today.

screenings.title: In My Skin
screenings.description: De Van writes, directs, and stars in this morbidly transfixing, at times suffocatingly intimate psychodrama from the high heady horrifying heyday of New French Extremity, playing Ester, a seemingly well adjusted Parisian career woman whose life changes dramatically after a chance injury to her leg one night sends her into a spiraling obsession with her body, in all of its frailty and friability, one that in time will become, in more than one sense, self-consuming. “As unrelenting an exploration of isolation and dissociation as Roman Polanski’s Repulsion… [A] remarkable debut film.” —The New York Times

screenings.title: The Straight Story
screenings.description: Leaving his Iowa home and sister Sissy Spacek behind, Alvin Straight (74-year-old Richard Farnsworth in a revelatory, Oscar-nominated performance) rides his lawnmower to Wisconsin to reunite with ailing brother Harry Dean Stanton. With an infectious warmth and characteristic attention to oddball specificity, Lynch’s enthralling road movie is one of the finest depictions of the Midwest in recent cinema.

screenings.title: Night of the Vamp-Friars
screenings.description: Roxy is an anthropology major at her local university as well as a DJ for the college’s radio station. One night, a listener calls into Roxy’s show to share a local legend about a hidden cemetery in the woods where a group of Friars who were killed and buried because the townspeople believed they were vampires. Thinking this would be a great topic for her thesis, Roxy convinces her friends in a punk band to head out into the woods for a weekend of camping in order to find the cemetery. After discovering that the legend of the cemetery is in fact real, blood is accidentally spilled on the hallowed ground, and the undead Friars rise from their graves in search of fresh victims to satisfy their blood lust.

screenings.title: Out of the Blue
screenings.description: Dennis Hopper’s hurricane-force domestic tragedy is the ’80s answer to EASY RIDER, following troubled youth subculture to its frightening, screaming, self-annihilating extreme. Just out of prison for drunk-driving his truck into a school bus, delinquent dad Don (Dennis Hopper) returns home to the planet’s most messed up family: heroin-addict wife Kathy (Sharon Farrell) and self-destructive, Elvis Presley– and Sid Vicious–obsessed rebel-punk daughter Cebe (Linda Manz), whose mantra is “disco sucks, kill all hippies.” Driven by the teenage Manz’s stunningly raw performance, OUT OF THE BLUE has lost none of the furiously nihilistic power that shocked audiences upon its premiere.

Nothing can go wrong, right?

screenings.title: Demon Seed
screenings.description: Dir. Donald Cammell. 1977, 94 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Julie Christie, Fritz Weaver, Gerrit Graham, and Robert Vaughn. Equal parts 2001: A Space Odyssey, Rosemary’s Baby, and Electric House, and showcasing an exquisite cybernetic psych-out sequence aided by visionary artist Jordan Belson and visual effects wizard Ron Hays, this post-humanist thriller unveils supercomputer Proteus IV: the latest invention of corporate monolith ICON that can cure leukemia, develop mining techniques, and ruminate on Buddhism with equal facility. When threatened, the hubristic machine seeks self-preservation by infiltrating the high-tech home of ICON’s lead scientist, trapping his wife and preparing her to propagate a new hybrid life form with his eponymous synthetic spermatozoa. Ticket buyers for Demon Seed can receive a 20% discount on tickets for The Brood with code OX20 Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. screenings.title: Viva Las Vegas + Learning from Learning from Las Vegas
screenings.description: All musically gifted race-driver Lucky Jackson (Elvis Presley) wants in Las Vegas is to score enough money for a new car motor so he can win the Grand Prix. When he encounters sexy swimming instructor Rusty (Ann-Margret), he considers staying around longer. After Lucky loses his winnings in the hotel pool, he’s forced to remain in Vegas long enough to win back his dough — but now he also wants to win Rusty’s heart. Unfortunately, so does his slick racing enemy, Elmo (Cesare Danova).
